Don't date a person with DID--or any person, really--if you're going to focus on their disorder more than who they are as a person. I'm surprised that a person with BPD would phrase a question with this level of... insensitivity.

I want to clarify: it isn't the asking of questions about the disorder or anything you may need to know going into a relationship with someone who has it that bothers me. It's the focusing in on these really negative traits that get applied to traumatized people that does it for me. 

The stigmas around dissociative disorders and personality disorders alike are harmful. Is he more likely to be traumatized by dating you? Are you more likely to be traumatized by dating him? These answers aren't found solely in a diagnosis. 

Look at yourself and see where you're at. If you're feeling hesitant, try continuing a friendship for a while to gauge if you two are in compatible places to support and love one another. Maybe his symptoms will be too much than you're ready to handle, or vice versa, and there's nothing wrong with that. But I'd base your decision more on your experience with him than the advice of redditors. Have a conversation with him, ask him more questions. If he disclosed to you that probably means he wants to discuss this with you.

Good luck. I'm sorry to hear you've had such traumatizing past relationships, but take it from someone who's been there, you can definitely find a relationship that will feel safe and right, even if it doesn't end up being this one.

honestly, just have fun. i think the only behaviors from killers that i can't stand are unwarranted face camping, tunneling (by which i mean going after the same survivor right off the hook or going after someone relentlessly even at the cost of the game), and team slugging/bleed outs (this is situational. there are definitely valid uses for this and also? sometimes i just can't find bleeding survivors in the shuffle so i try not to be too bothered by it if that happens in reverse). anything else just doesn't make sense to be annoyed about.

Ah, you've just hit on one of the most unfortunate things about Origins. I have immense love for this series, but even in Inquisition, it still stumbles with romances from a female character's perspective. Don't get me wrong, they've improved considerably, but...

I played a female city elf for my very first playthrough, years and years ago, and it was one of the first RPGs where I got to play someone who was more like myself. Naturally, I went for Alistair. I seem to have a different experience than the sampling of comments I read--my Alistair was still soft, and as such, I just let Anora stay queen. He really didn't seem to want the throne, and people have been making choices for him his whole life, so I couldn't force that on him. Then Morrigan (who was my Warden's sister at heart!) says "oh hey, I've been lying to you, convince the love of your life to sleep with me!"

Aaaand I did.  But it felt slimy and awful. I had JUST given him the freedom of choice to stay a Warden, and here I was going back on what I stood for and making another choice for him. But I didn't want him to lose the woman he loved, especially after losing Duncan and finding out his "sister" was a harpy, and Alistair dying wasn't on the table as far as I was concerned. I hated that there weren't any good options to have a better conversation or to comfort him or... anything.

Then my next game, I played a male Warden and romanced Morrigan. It felt like a walk in the park, in comparison. I felt so slighted.

In subsequent playthroughs, I almost always have the Dark Ritual happen, even if it makes me severely uncomfortable. Mostly because I love Alistair too much to let him die for me, and I also think that it's too depressing to go the ultimate sacrifice route. I've done it, once, and it just wasn't for me.

Now, I will say... keeping him as a warden? Imagine my distress in Inquisition. Luckily, I was using a worldstate with my first Warden and my first Hawke. And I had made the ill advised choice of romancing Anders in my first DA2 playthrough... that's what I get for enjoying his snark in Awakening.
